title: Cap. IV Arg. 7 Sol: double praeordinatio — intention and execution both declare mercy and justice
pass_a_gloss: Solution. In the Divine mind one ought to conceive a double praeordination as to the Elect: one, which contains the order of intention; the other, which contains the order of execution: But both serve for declaring the Divine mercy and justice. For example; That God before the foundations of the world were laid decreed to love Jacob and Peter, and to have mercy on the same in the donation of special grace and eternal life; but to pass by Esau and Judas in this designation to the infallible attainment of life and grace, and to appoint those hardened in their sins to just condemnation: in these decrees, I say, there is contained a certain abyss of mercy and justice, for penetrating which no sharpness of human genius suffices. But now that the same God in his word has opened that he has decreed to save all believers, to damn all unbelievers, and that (on the day of judgment) when it has come to execution, in fact he damns Esau and Judas, saves Jacob and Peter: he also expresses an excellent and singular specimen of the Divine mercy and justice.
pass_b_english: Sol. In God's mind regarding the elect, conceive a double praeordination: one of intention, one of execution — both serve to declare divine mercy and justice. Example: before the world's foundations God decreed to love Jacob and Peter and have mercy on them in special grace and eternal life; to pass by Esau and Judas for that infallible attainment of life and grace, and appoint those hardened in their sins to just condemnation — an abyss of mercy and justice no human wit can pierce. And that the same God has opened in his word that he decreed to save all believers and damn all unbelievers, and that on judgment day he in fact damns Esau and Judas and saves Jacob and Peter — that too is a singular specimen of divine mercy and justice.
source_text: Sol. In mente Divina concipere oportet quoad Electos praeordinationem duplicem: unam, quae ordinem intentionis continet; alteram, quae ordinem exsecutionis: Utraque autem inservit declarandae misericordiae et justitiae Divinae. Exempli causa; Quod Deus ante jacta mundi fundamenta decreverit Jacobum et Petrum diligere, ac eorundem in donatione gratiae specialis ac vitae aeternae misereri; Esavum autem et Judam in hac designatione ad infallibilem vitae gratiaeque consecutionem praeterire, atque in peccatis suis obfirmatos justae condemnationi deputare: in hisce, inquam, decretis continetur abyssus quaedam misericordiae et justitiae, cujus penetrandae nulla acies humani ingenii sufficit. Jam vero quod idem Deus in verbo suo patefecerit, se decrevisse omnes credentes salvare, omnes incredulos damnare, quodque (in die judicii) cum ad exsecutionem ventum fuerit, de facto Esavum et Judam damnet, Jacobum et Petrum servet: exprimit etiam misericordiae justitiaeque Divinae egregium ac singulare specimen.
